findings.F1: In the rising, agitated profile, the stretch above the 20-day average, in daily-swing units, is not followed by a giveback: the day-clustered slope of the drift-removed 5-day return on the stretch is +0.034 (t 0.91, 304 cases, 121 days), and the quintiles rise rather than fall (strength -0.10 in the lowest, +0.34 in the fourth with t 2.25, +0.06 in the highest), in line with the verdict's -0.065 strength.
findings.F2: In the choppy profile (60-day return between -10 % and +10 %), the stretch from the 20-day average in daily-swing units carries forward. The slope of the drift-removed return on the stretch is +0.170 over 5 days (t 2.36, 125 cases, 65 days) and +0.176 over 10 days (t 3.08, 62 cases, 30 days). Over 5 days, the lowest stretch quintile has a strength of -1.00 (t -2.97, 16 cases) and the highest +0.31 (22 cases).
findings.F3: The choppy continuation is graded on both sides of the average over 5 days. Cases below the average have a strength of -0.43 (60 cases, slope +0.26, t 1.10) and cases above it +0.12 (65 cases, slope +0.13, t 1.71).

findings.F5: In the rising, calm profile the stretch also continues: the slope is +0.127 over 10 days (t 3.21, 90 cases, 30 days) and +0.081 over 5 days (t 2.00). This repeats 058-03.e1 ("calm rise stretch ten days") and 035-01.b1, which the map already holds.

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the further a coin's close stands from its 20-day average, measured in units of its daily swing over the last 20 days, the further the coin keeps moving in that same direction over the next 10 days: up when it stands above the average, down when it stands below it.
ideas.consequence: In a coin going nowhere over two months, a stretch from its average that is large for its current swing marks the start of a move to follow, not one to fade, on both the long and the short side.
ideas.name: choppy stretch continues ten days
